items.text: Spring storms can bring lightning strikes and power surges, which occasionally contribute to electrical fires in homes and outbuildings.

items.title: Summer
items.text: Hot, dry Texas summers increase wildfire risk in surrounding areas and put added strain on HVAC and electrical systems working overtime.

items.title: Fall
items.text: As temperatures cool, increased use of heating equipment and fireplaces raises the risk of house fires from improper use or maintenance.

items.title: Winter

sections.heading: Fire Damage Restoration FAQs for New Braunfels Homeowners

items.q: How quickly should I call for fire damage restoration in New Braunfels, TX?
items.a: As soon as the fire department has cleared the property as safe to enter, contacting a restoration team promptly helps limit the spread of smoke and soot damage.

items.q: Will my homeowner's insurance cover fire damage restoration?
items.a: Coverage depends on your specific policy. We provide detailed documentation of the damage and work performed to support your claim, though approval and coverage decisions are made by your insurance company.

items.q: Can all fire and smoke damage be fully repaired?
items.a: Many fire-damaged areas and belongings can be cleaned and restored, but some materials affected by heavy smoke, heat, or fire suppression water may need to be replaced rather than repaired.

items.q: Is it safe to enter a fire-damaged home on my own?
items.a: Re-entering a fire-damaged structure can involve risks from weakened flooring, electrical hazards, or compromised air quality. Always wait for clearance from fire officials before entering, and let trained professionals handle assessment and cleanup.
